initial_observation.encounter_context: admitted to the hospital with a 12-hour history of sudden-onset abdominal pain
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: She had an elevated serum phosphate level and metabolic lactic acidosis with leukocytosis and inflammatory signs, but abdominal contrast-enhanced CT revealed no specific signs of bowel ischemia.

evidence_items.source_text: Upon admission, her O2 saturation was 98% with the administration of 4 L of oxygen, and her limbs were cold with mottled skin. Arterial blood gas testing showed metabolic lactic acidosis (pH 7.110, pCO2 32 mmHg, HCO3 9.5 mmol/L, lactate 9.1 mmol/L). Further laboratory investigations revealed leukocytosis, marked inflammatory signs, and renal dysfunction (Table). Furthermore, a remarkable elevation in serum phosphate level (14.4 mg/dL), disproportionate to the renal dysfunction, was noted.

Abdominal contrast-enhanced CT revealed a dilated colon and small intestine, containing fluids. However, complete or closed-loop obstruction was not observed. Free air, ascites, and other signs of an ischemic bowel, such as the absence of bowel wall enhancement, pneumatosis intestinalis, hepatic portal venous gas, and bowel wall thickening, were not seen (Fig. 1).
One hour after admission, her systolic blood pressure decreased from 139 to 60 mmHg and she went into shock.

Although there was no clear evidence of bowel obstruction, ischemia, or infarction, the patient underwent emergency laparotomy after six hours of intensive resuscitation. The ileum and whole colon, except for the sigmoid, were discontinuously necrotic despite pulsation of the superior mesenteric artery (Fig. 2). There was no bowel obstruction.

The patient was diagnosed with NOMI. Therefore, ileal resection, subtotal colectomy, and jejunostomy were performed. The residual jejunal length was 120 cm. After surgery, the patient recovered, and her serum phosphate level immediately returned to its normal range.

hidden_reference.final_diagnosis_verbatim: The patient was diagnosed with NOMI.
